summary: Willamette NF ground L-4 cab built in 1934, with lookouts reported in 1921 and 1929. Removed or destroyed in 1962. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: Ground L-4 cab, 14 x 14 ft per the Forest Lookouts page
facts.status_note: Cab removed in 1962 per the register and Forest Lookouts page; firelookout.com says destroyed that year

staffing.status: lookouts named in 1921 and 1929 newspaper items

events.note: July 1921 item says C.E. Harritt was to start as lookout for the Santiam reserve at Outerson Park; unclear whether that is the summit
September 1929 item names Paul Bayless as Outerson Mountain lookout
Ground L-4 cab; register credits the USFS, Forest Lookouts page credits the CCC with a 14 x 14 ft house
Register and Forest Lookouts say removed; firelookout.com says destroyed

evidence.supports: location: Willamette National Forest, Marion County, Oregon
1934 ground L-4 cab built by USFS; removed in 1962
evidence.quote: In 1934 the USFS built a ground L-4 cab, which was removed in 1962.

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Forest Service

evidence.supports: July 1921 item: C.E. Harritt to be lookout at Outerson Park
evidence.quote: C.E. Harritt left yesterday for Outerson Park where he will commence his duties at once a lookout for the Santiam National Forest reserve.

evidence.quote: the old Boulder Ridge Trail connected the Outerson Mountain Lookout with the Triangulation Peak Lookout

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the Forest Lookouts page say the cab was removed in 1962. firelookout.com says it was destroyed that year. The story reports both and does not choose.
The register credits the U.S. Forest Service. The Forest Lookouts page credits the Civilian Conservation Corps with building a 14 x 14 ft lookout house. Both are named in the story.

sources.title: Phantom Trails of the Santiam Canyon

notes_for_editor: No source describes the site today. The 1921 item names Outerson Park, which may not be the summit; the story now says the 1921 item does not state whether Outerson Park is the summit. The 1929 and 1921 entries come from newspaper clippings as transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page. The 1962 fate is disputed (removed vs destroyed). Brief record (gone, ground, registered 2010-09-19) checks out; no corrections.
